Reused from operator-level research completed in an earlier phase of this project (twoai_dc_operators row: DataBank, operator-level status: complete).

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] DataBank was founded in 2005 and is headquartered in Dallas, Texas. Digital Bridge, now DigitalBridge Group, acquired the company in July 2016 and used it to launch a broader data center investment platform. Trade press reports DigitalBridge later sold a stake in DataBank to Swiss Life Asset Management for approximately $1.2 billion, a transaction this entry records from secondary reporting rather than a confirmed primary source.

DataBanks own company-history page describes growth to more than 65 data centers across more than 27 markets following a series of acquisitions, without stating a precise current total. Among those acquisitions, a January 2022 press release describes DataBank buying Houston-area data centers from CyrusOne, another operator separately tracked in this registry, an example of consolidation moving facilities directly between two operators already profiled here.

The registry here tracks 14 DataBank facilities across six states, California, Nevada, New York, Texas, Utah, and Virginia. As a DigitalBridge-sponsored colocation platform built substantially through acquisition, including at least one purchase directly from CyrusOne, DataBanks history is a useful cross-check for this registrys later facility-level work: any DataBank facility in the Houston, Texas area should be checked against former CyrusOne records for a possible former_operator relationship rather than treated as an independent new build. This facility is recorded under the operator name Databank in this registry, treated as the same entity as DataBank researched at the operator level. This research was carried out at the operator level in an earlier phase of this project.

reading.body:
Databank LGA3 is located in Rockland County, New York, roughly 25 miles north of New York City. The facility has no published power capacity, IT load, cooling capacity, or other specifications available on the operator's spec page. Without those figures, the campus cannot be assessed as a constraint on AI compute scaling.

New York State has 31 mapped data center facilities in this registry, of which only one other publishes a power specification. The state total of published capacity is 3 megawatts, making Databank LGA3 rank second among disclosed facilities statewide by that measure, though that ranking reflects the absence of published data rather than the presence of significant capacity. Most mapped facilities in New York publish no figures at all.

Databank is a colocation operator with 14 tracked facilities across six states. The operator's history includes acquisition of facilities from other tracked operators, notably CyrusOne. Without published specifications for this Rockland County site, its role in serving AI workloads cannot be determined from available data.
